subject: physics_2
question_text: In which bias can a zener diode be used as voltage regulator?

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Paper-II bank the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers, so neither check was run. TRANSCRIPTION: the book prints 'In whihc bias can a zener diode be used as voltage regulator' — 'whihc' is corrected to 'which' and the missing question mark is added.

recall_prompt: Say which bias a zener diode is used in as a regulator, and what stays constant there.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The bias
lines: A zener diode is used as a voltage
steps.margin_note: First mark. One word carries it: reverse.
steps.why: A zener diode in forward bias behaves like any other diode, so nothing about it would regulate. Its special property — a sharp, repeatable breakdown at a fixed voltage — exists only in reverse bias.
common_mistakes: Answering forward bias. In forward bias a zener diode is an ordinary diode.
Answering 'both biases'. Only the reverse breakdown region regulates.

recall.must_convey: That the zener diode is used in reverse bias.

steps.memory_tip: Every other diode is used forward. The zener is the reverse one.

steps.label: Why reverse bias
lines: In reverse bias the diode is worked in
the breakdown region. There the voltage
across it stays nearly constant at the
zener voltage while the current through
it changes over a wide range.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Name the breakdown region and say the voltage stays constant while the current changes.
steps.why: Regulation means holding the output voltage fixed while the input voltage or the load current changes. Only a device whose voltage barely moves while its current moves a lot can do that, and the reverse breakdown region of a zener diode is exactly that region of the characteristic.
common_mistakes: Saying the current stays constant. It is the VOLTAGE that stays constant.
Leaving out the word breakdown. The regulating region is the reverse breakdown region.

recall.must_convey: That in reverse breakdown the voltage across the diode stays nearly constant while the current varies.
accept: in breakdown the voltage stays constant
current changes but voltage does not

steps.memory_tip: Voltage flat, current free — that flat piece of the curve is the regulator.

insider_note: Two words earn the first mark, but the second mark needs the reason — constant voltage in the breakdown region — so do not stop at 'reverse bias'.
